statement.note_ascii: tau_R dI_R/dt + L_R I_R = S_R + eta_R

definitions.I_R: retained turbulence state (a vector/Hilbert/finite-graph state, not a scalar)
definitions.tau_R: positive scalar restoration time / relaxation inertia, tau_R > 0
definitions.L_R: the retained restoration operator: declared as a graph Laplacian / linearized restoration operator, positive semidefinite on the declared state space, zero-mode policy declared
definitions.S_R: structural source/drive (mean shear, energy injection, boundary forcing, cascade input, ...)
definitions.eta_R: unresolved residual/stochastic disturbance; the source's own claim_boundary states this must be logged, bounded, and tested, never treated as a free error bin

parents.evidence: Identical functional shape to the registered Finite-Memory Laplacian/Telegraph Generator (weld/S.01.v1: A := L_R + Gamma; ds/dt = -A s + J, i.e. ds/dt + (L_R+Gamma) s = J), here applied to a new domain (turbulence structural state I_R) instead of the social-instability state s. This is a domain instance of the same first-order retained-response law, not a new law.

The source's own definition of L_R ('graph Laplacian / scale Laplacian / linearized restoration operator / positive operator, positive semidefinite, zero-mode policy declared') matches, in words, IDM/Genesis root EQ-008's canonical definition L_R := D_W - W (weighted-degree minus retained-adjacency, a full operator on a multimode state). The source paper does not itself cite EQ-008; this attachment records a structural match found at intake, not an author claim.

does_not_resolve.reason: Genesis root row T2 ('endogenous state-dependent L_R[I_R], where the operator itself depends on the state it is acting on') is the harder, still-open case. This equation's own stated assumption set explicitly keeps 'L_R time-independent' (solution_form_linear_time_invariant) -- it is the easier linear/state-independent sub-case, not an attempted or claimed resolution of T2. State this honestly if the entry is ever cited near T2.
